findings.title: Finite-value constraints accepted infinity under another spelling
findings.impact: A calibration literal "1e309"^^xsd:double passed the lexical blacklist although its numeric value is infinite. This can contaminate georeferencing or calibrated values.
findings.evidence: Both positive and negative overflow spellings passed before the fix. Nine pySHACL boundary cases now pass; Jena independently verifies nonfinite rejection and finite extremes.
findings.action: Added numeric bounds excluding both infinities while preserving valid finite extremes and signed zero. No-data NaN remains allowed in its separate contract.

findings.title: Band-index uniqueness confused RDF identity with numeric equality
findings.impact: Two bands could both occupy numeric index 1 when one index was xsd:integer and the other xsd:unsignedInt.
findings.evidence: The counterexample conformed before correction. It now fails in pySHACL and Jena.
findings.action: Join the two index values independently and compare them numerically. Band resources themselves are compared by RDF term identity.

findings.title: Malformed coefficient lists hid duplicate equal-valued literals
findings.impact: Two different lexical double literals with equal numeric value could both be rdf:first on one coefficient cell. The list was not well formed, yet value inequality failed to detect it.
findings.evidence: A valid 20-cell vector passes; adding a second equal-valued but distinct rdf:first now fails. Repeated values in separate cells remain legal.
findings.action: Use sameTerm for list multiplicity checks in raster and spatial-reference constraints. Numeric equality remains appropriate for quantities, not graph cardinality.

findings.title: Compression framing needed an explicit zlib concept
findings.impact: The documented raw DEFLATE meaning and engine dispatch disagreed. A profile identifier did not reliably identify the byte framing.
findings.evidence: The raw RFC 1951 dispatch regression failed before correction. The register now has 24 codec/compression concepts and the PNG resource uses Zlib.
findings.action: Added menc:Zlib; retained distinct Deflate and Gzip meanings; documented the required migration for profiles relying on the old alias.

findings.title: Complete references are synchronized with canonical RDF
findings.impact: Hand-maintained descriptions can drift from the vocabulary and its shapes, especially across imported aspects.
findings.evidence: 731 named resources, 93 named shapes and 35 modules pass annotation, reference, fragment-link and embedded-RDF checks. There are 16 specification gates.
findings.action: Keep generation and the completeness gate in CI. Term coverage establishes documentation presence, not independent semantic review of every definition.

findings.title: GDAL inventory is not binary interoperability evidence
findings.impact: A vocabulary can describe a format family while its parser, payload decoder or semantic output remains unsupported.
findings.evidence: The inventory pins 246 GDAL documentation pages and distinguishes capability levels. It does not supply a driver-by-driver binary corpus or independently compared outputs.
findings.action: Build versioned corpora for representative GDAL families, compare metadata and decoded values against GDAL, and record tested driver/version/options and negative cases.

findings.title: Semantic competency evidence remains narrower than vocabulary coverage
findings.impact: Generated definitions and broad module scope notes cannot establish that all combinations of terms model real formats correctly.
findings.evidence: Geospatial tests cover 40 semantic cases and 121 exact affine round trips, plus the new numeric cases. Equivalent depth is not established for all 731 resources.
findings.action: Add concrete positive/negative examples and competency questions for packaging, security-register bindings, timing, bit packing and compound datasets. Seek independent ontology review.

findings.title: Working drafts need a release and compatibility process
findings.impact: Stricter shape validation can reject previously accepted graphs, even when term IRIs remain stable.
findings.evidence: Raster/spatial-reference drafts are versioned and this pass records migrations. Live namespace negotiation, archived releases and external consumer compatibility were not tested.
findings.action: Publish immutable release artifacts, validate dereferencing/content negotiation, and maintain a compatibility corpus per released version.

findings.title: Sizes and repeat counts narrowed before validation
findings.impact: A fixed size of 4,294,967,297 bytes wrapped to one byte. Fractional counts were truncated, and a large count could trigger a large allocation before reading input.
findings.evidence: The fixed-size and count counterexamples failed the new expected-correctness tests before this pass. Exact conversion and uint64/count tests now pass.
findings.action: Validate integral finite values before narrowing; bound byte/string allocations by remaining input; start repetition storage with a modest capacity. Existing recovery semantics are retained.

findings.title: Array access could return wrong signed values or aliased cells
findings.impact: Signed -1 decoded as 255; uint32/uint64 values narrowed silently. Missing/extra indices, invalid logical coordinates and overflowing strides could access an unrelated byte.
findings.evidence: Pre-fix tests reproduced signedness, index and stride failures. Final tests cover uint64 maximum, float64 precision, bounds, rank and truncated cells.
findings.action: Added exact getInteger/getLong and getDouble accessors. Narrowing getInt fails outside its range. Checked long arithmetic and complete-cell bounds protect every array access.

findings.title: Inflater termination could mean partial success or endless waiting
findings.impact: A truncated compressed block returned partial data; a preset-dictionary request could repeatedly make no progress. Native resources were not released on every failure path.
findings.evidence: Every truncated prefix of sample zlib/raw DEFLATE payloads is now rejected. Dictionary, empty-stream, output-budget and trailing-byte cases pass.
findings.action: Require stream completion, fail on missing dictionaries or stalled progress, and release native resources in finally. Correct RFC 1951 and Deflate dispatch to raw framing.

findings.title: Unsupported DLV features disappeared during IR lowering
findings.impact: Chunk addressing, conditional layouts, packed-cell declarations or dynamic strides could be expressed in RDF but were absent from the IR, leaving a misleading ordinary-layout interpretation.
findings.evidence: The compiler now rejects the known unsupported declarations with their names. A supported contiguous layout still compiles; the regression tests cover both paths.
findings.action: Keep this explicit capability gate until the relevant IR, parser, writer and semantic-output support exist. This is safe rejection, not implementation of those formats.

findings.title: Unsigned 64-bit output became zero
findings.impact: The writer converted only Number values; Kotlin ULong values produced by the parser were not Numbers and fell back to zero. Small-width integer output also wrapped out-of-range inputs.
findings.evidence: The uint64 maximum now survives parse/write exactly. Fractional, nonfinite, nonnumeric, negative unsigned and overflowing integer values are rejected.
findings.action: Check the exact integer against its signed/unsigned width before writing its bit pattern. Float conversion and bitfield writing have separate contracts and are not certified by these tests.

findings.title: Decoded-byte limits do not bound a whole parse
findings.impact: A small compressed input can create a large result. Multiple blocks, recursive structures or zero-byte repetitions can still consume excessive total memory or CPU.
findings.evidence: All built-in codecs enforce configurable per-block output limits; the core default is 64 MiB. Tests use small budgets and valid empty streams.
findings.action: Add a shared parse budget for total emitted bytes/nodes, nesting depth and operations, with cancellation propagated through decoding and evaluation. Keep worker isolation at service boundaries.

findings.title: Writer symmetry and large-output behavior remain incomplete
findings.impact: Correct scalar output does not make the writer the inverse of every parser feature. Explicit offsets/alignment and bounded structures are not replayed by the current sequential writer; capacity estimates and unchecked size conversion are additional limits.
findings.evidence: Source inspection: writeStruct walks fields sequentially; estimateCapacity assigns a small estimate to byte-array values; resolveSize still narrows values. These paths are not covered by the new scalar integer fix.
findings.action: Introduce explicit writer capability rejection, checked sizing and a growing or streaming output sink. Require round trips for every supported feature and negative tests for unsupported profiles before advertising general write support.

findings.title: Description validation is distinct from emitted-instance validation
findings.impact: A valid profile does not establish that the produced raster, geometry or timing graph conforms to all applicable semantic shapes.
findings.evidence: ProfileLoader explicitly limits its default shape graph to BDDO/Core/DLV. New Jena tests opt into raster shapes; this is not automatic semantic validation on every run.
findings.action: Add a separately named emitted-graph validation stage with declared entailment, shape selection and provenance. Preserve the distinction in API results.

findings.title: Independent parser and writer assurance is still limited
findings.impact: A large unit suite can share assumptions with the implementation, and it does not establish support for every registered codec or GDAL format.
findings.evidence: 431 core and 223 HDL tests pass. New Jena/pySHACL checks give independent evidence for selected semantic constraints, not all binary parsing paths.
findings.action: Add differential parsing, property-based boundary tests, mutation corpora and fuzzing; expand codec implementations only with framing-specific fixtures and resource limits.

findings.title: Mutable sample bytes invalidated stored digests and cached results
findings.impact: A caller could mutate the original or returned byte array after save, changing content while keeping the stored SHA-256 and run references.
findings.evidence: The new repository test failed before correction. It now mutates ingress, save return, single lookup and list lookup arrays without altering storage.
findings.action: Store and return defensive byte copies, and verify declared length and SHA-256 against the stored snapshot. This protects in-process identity; durable content storage remains open.

findings.title: File and format identities could be overwritten
findings.impact: Saving an existing file ID replaced the bytes referenced by historical runs; replacing a format could change the workspace owner of existing versions.
findings.evidence: Both overwrite counterexamples failed before the fix and now reject replacement while preserving the first resource.
findings.action: Reject duplicate file/format IDs. A future persistence layer must enforce equivalent unique constraints transactionally.

findings.title: Validation and viewing now limit decoded blocks
findings.impact: The interactive input limit alone did not stop compression expansion inside either execution path.
findings.evidence: An integration test supplies a small compressed payload expanding beyond 8 MiB; validation and viewing both fail with the budget explanation.
findings.action: Both paths use the same 8 MiB per-block limit. Whole-run quotas, cancellation and isolated workers are still needed for hostile or resource-heavy profiles.

findings.title: Unexpected HTTP 422 responses could masquerade as successful data
findings.impact: The shared client treated every 422 as a typed success. Error objects could reach screens expecting a compile result or collection, while ordinary errors displayed raw JSON.
findings.evidence: New API tests check rejected compile requests, readable error explanations and structured INVALID publication diagnostics. Both .ts and .tsx tests are discovered.
findings.action: Only publication accepts a structured 422 result. Other failing statuses reject with a readable server explanation; CSRF handling remains in the shared client.

findings.title: In-memory storage cannot provide durable service guarantees
findings.impact: A restart loses stored formats, versions, runs and findings. In-process synchronization does not coordinate multiple service instances.
findings.evidence: The repository adapters use in-memory maps. Publish concurrency is protected within one process only.
findings.action: Introduce durable transactional metadata, immutable object storage, schema migrations, uniqueness constraints, and backup/restore tests. Demonstrate crash recovery before a production readiness claim.

findings.title: Authentication currently protects one configured workspace
findings.impact: The implemented deployment does not provide tenant-aware authorization, per-project roles or distributed execution isolation.
findings.evidence: Authentication, CSRF and foreign-object tests pass. WorkspaceAccess uses a server-configured workspace ID for the deployment.
findings.action: Retain this supported deployment scope. For a multi-tenant product, derive authorization from authenticated memberships and isolate storage and worker execution by tenant.

findings.title: Browser accessibility and operational performance need acceptance evidence
findings.impact: Component tests cannot establish real screen-reader behavior, responsive rendering, actual keyboard focus across navigation, or latency under concurrent runs.
findings.evidence: Six frontend tests and the production build are checked in this pass. No manual browser, screen-reader, load, restart or distributed deployment test was performed.
findings.action: Run keyboard and screen-reader walkthroughs, responsive screenshots, realistic corpus timing and concurrent-run load tests. Keep the 1 MiB viewer limit visible until larger-file interaction is implemented.

findings.title: Engine changes are pinned and the patch can be regenerated
findings.impact: An application tested against an edited sibling engine is not reproducible if new files are omitted from its delivery patch.
findings.evidence: The refresh tool includes tracked changes plus new source/test files, checks the pinned base, and validates reverse application. npm audit reports zero known npm vulnerabilities at review time; no equivalent JVM advisory audit was performed.
findings.action: Run the new patch check locally after engine edits and run the existing clean-checkout CI. Upstream the patch into a versioned engine release; remote CI execution is not claimed here.
